skill.name: remotion-render
skill.description: Render React and Remotion TSX components as configurable videos through the inference.sh service.
skill.summary: Turn Remotion components into rendered videos with configurable dimensions, frame rate, duration, codec, and props.
skill.author: inferen-sh

security_audit.summary: Most external-command detections are Markdown formatting, code fences, or source examples and are false positives. Eight examples invoke external tooling, one image loads remotely, and the workflow sends supplied code and props to inference.sh.

remediation.issue: The workflow submits user code and props to an external rendering service.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval before submission and warn users to remove secrets or confidential data from source and props.

remediation.issue: Installation examples use npx skill commands without pinned versions or immutable references.
remediation.suggestion: Pin trusted package and skill versions, document their source, and require confirmation before installation.

remediation.issue: The documentation embeds an image from a remote inference.sh URL.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the image with the skill or clearly disclose that viewing the documentation can contact the remote host.

content.value_statement: Turning React animation code into shareable video requires a rendering pipeline. This skill submits Remotion components to inference.sh and returns rendered video output.
actual_capabilities: Submits default-exported React and Remotion TSX components for video rendering.
Configures video width, height, frame rate, duration, and codec.
Passes structured props into a rendered React component.
Uses Remotion timing, interpolation, spring, sequence, audio, video, and image APIs.
Shows CLI, Python SDK, and streaming progress workflows.
Returns a rendered video reference from the inference.sh service.
limitations: Requires an inference.sh account, belt authentication, and network access.
Sends component source and props to an external rendering service.
Only documented React and Remotion imports are supported.
Rendering cost, queue time, output retention, and service limits are not documented here.

use_cases.title: Create Product Animations
use_cases.description: Render reusable product announcements from React components with configurable titles, colors, and timing.

use_cases.title: Produce Data Videos
use_cases.description: Pass structured values into a component to generate consistent counters, reports, or metric animations.

use_cases.title: Automate Motion Assets
use_cases.description: Generate repeatable social and campaign videos from approved Remotion templates.

prompt_templates.title: Render Simple Text
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a three-second Remotion video with centered fade-in text. Use 1920 by 1080 pixels at 30 frames per second.

prompt_templates.title: Animate Provided Values
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Remotion component that receives title and percentage props. Animate the percentage from zero and render a five-second square video.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Sequenced Scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Render three timed scenes with Sequence, spring transitions, and consistent typography. Use 60 frames per second and provide progress updates.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Production Render
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Remotion TSX for unsupported imports, secret values, timing errors, and layout issues. Then render with my approved dimensions, duration, and codec.

output_examples.input: Render a three-second title fade at 1920 by 1080 pixels and 30 frames per second.
output_examples.output: A completed render with a video reference and the requested duration, dimensions, and frame rate.

output_examples.input: Animate a percentage from zero to 100 in a five-second square video.
output: A square rendered video showing the animated percentage.
Streaming progress updates while the remote render runs.
A final video reference after completion.

output_examples.input: Render a title card using supplied title and subtitle props.
output_examples.output: A reusable title-card video populated with the supplied text values.

best_practices: Remove secrets and confidential values before submitting code or props.
Test timing and layout at a lower resolution before starting a final render.
Specify dimensions, frame rate, duration, and codec explicitly for repeatable output.
anti_patterns: Do not submit untrusted TSX without reviewing its imports and behavior.
Do not place credentials, private URLs, or personal data in component source or props.
Do not install related skills or packages without verifying their publisher and version.

faq.question: What does this skill render?
faq.answer: It renders default-exported React components that use supported React and Remotion APIs.

faq.question: What output does it produce?
faq.answer: The documented workflow returns a video reference from the inference.sh rendering service.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Yes. Rendering uses inference.sh and requires authenticated network access through belt or the Python SDK.

faq.question: Can I pass data into the component?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide structured props, but remove secrets and sensitive information before submission.

faq.question: Which render settings can I control?
faq.answer: You can set width, height, frame rate, duration, composition identifier, props, and codec.

faq.question: Can it report rendering progress?
faq.answer: Yes. The Python SDK example streams progress updates and returns the video reference when rendering completes.
